item.title: 1. From Spiking Neural Networks to Biologically Inspired Computation
1.4 Excitation, Inhibition, and Winner-Take-All Competition
item.description: Excitation, Inhibition, and Winner-Take-All Competition A Leaky Integrate-and-Fire neuron can accumulate incoming spikes, reach its threshold, emit a spike, and reset.

item.title: 2.1 Measuring Inference Latency
item.description: Measuring Inference Latency Once an SNN has received spikes and produced a decision, we can ask a practical question: how long did that decision take? Imagine an input stream in which a stimulus begins at a known instant-perhaps the first event in a recorded sample.

item.title: 2.2 Spike Count and Inference Energy
item.description: Spike Count and Inference Energy Once stimulus onset has been placed on a timeline, the network’s response can be followed timestep by timestep.

item.title: 2.3 Accuracy and Normalized Energy Efficiency
item.description: Accuracy and Normalized Energy Efficiency Once a network has turned an input into a predicted class label, imagine checking a batch of 100 predictions against the correct labels.

item.title: 2.4 Convergence Epoch and Training Progress
item.description: Convergence Epoch and Training Progress Once accuracy has been tracked across training epochs, the resulting learning curve shows how performance develops over time.
